notes: organic mantle during phase A: Giuseppe -> Aaron d20

convoLines.text: "Pantry's thin and getting thinner. Will you forage with me tomorrow? Two pairs of eyes, twice the ground."
"I did the count twice. The count doesn't change. I know where the blackberry grows thick — come with me and we'll fill packs before dark."
Move next to your partner, on the same side of the Haven door.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Giuseppe always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
"I work alone. Nothing personal. ...It's a little personal."
You show them Ghost Pipe — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Can I tell you something? I know who took the extra rations but won't say."
"Walk my trap line with me? Extra hands, extra eyes."
"I buried this before the Scattering. Seemed stupid to keep it secret." Wanjiru digs up a wrapped bundle — food, still good. (+1780 kcal to the pantry.)
"an old trapline — I'll show you on the map sometime. It's real."
"a burned farmhouse — I'll show you on the map sometime. It's real."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Right, so — Still on what they confided."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
You show them Ghost Pipe — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"...Anyway. What did you want to ask?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Giuseppe owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
"Right. Go on, then."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"People are smiling. I forgot what that looked like."
"Come get air with me. I need to think out loud."
You walk to the ridge with Siobhan. Nothing much there — but they talk the whole way, and you learn the shape of them a little better.
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on cheer."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"I work alone. Nothing personal. ...It's a little personal."
"Good times. What did you want to talk about?"
"You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Since Giuseppe died... I keep expecting to see Giuseppe at the fire. Stupid."
You show them White Oak Acorns — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Nobody says Giuseppe's name right yet. We will. Give it a few days."
"Anyway — I should get back to it. Good talking, though."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"We never finished talking about what they confided — we wandered off it, 4 days back. '...Anyway. What did you want to ask?' We still owe what's been happening a proper ending, too."
"Take your time."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"As I said — Still on what they confided."
You show them Black Walnut — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Don't tell anyone I told you. What's on your mind?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Last time things were different. They always are." "Giuseppe is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
"We bury, we grieve, we keep going. There's no step four."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"This was good." They mean it.
"About the pantry run — I hate to ask twice, but it's still open. Will you?"
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "They took you — Wheel of Teeth, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"That's... pretty much all of it, honestly."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"When's the last time you really laughed? You'd know about that."
"Stealing joy. I like that. We should steal more of it."
"Watch for this: The grass stops moving the way wind moves it. Sweeps Week, every time. Dawn and dusk, that's when it's out."
"Three days ago. Someone dropped a whole basket of tubers and we just stood there laughing. It wasn't even funny. It was the standing there."
"Why do you ask? Still on the last time you laughed."
"All right. Thank you for asking."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Same story, different day. The ending hasn't changed."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"A full belly makes everything else possible. It's the foundation. I build foundations."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"We're eating through stores faster than we replace them. Come forage with me tomorrow — two of us can fill packs."
"The stores won't stretch past tomorrow, and I'm not choosing who eats. Nobody's worked the east treeline in days. We'll fill packs before dark."
Your partner is inside the Haven hall. Go through the door to meet them.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "You saw it too, right? The Informant. Tell me I didn't imagine the lights."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on what's been happening."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"Right. Go on, then."
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"You told me about the stolen laugh — someone tripping over nothing. Have you stolen any more since?"
"All right. Thank you for telling me."
"This one — Masoor Lentil. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on that personal stuff. Don't look away from this."
"Sure — what's on your mind? Just... be straight with me."
"You want to know about that? Okay." "They took Ursula and Nurdaulet — The Informant, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
"Ask me tomorrow. Everything changes by tomorrow."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Count the fireflies with me? No reason. Just — count them."
"It crouches low, tail lashing once, twice. That's The Mountain Lord telling you it's about to move. Dawn and dusk, that's when it's out."
"Watch for this: It drops its head and paws the earth — once, twice — and the dust comes up in a wall. Dustboar, every time. It hunts by day — watch the open ground."
Their eyes do the math before their mouth does. You can see the calculation happening.
"I wasn't a hunting guide. I was a lifeguard. I thought if you believed that, you'd trust me faster. I'm sorry. Or I'm supposed to be."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
Your partner is inside the Haven hall. Go through the door to meet them.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"I did the count twice. The count doesn't change. Meet me at the far treeline, past the rocks and we'll fill packs before dark."
"Yeah? What's up?"
"Good question." "I could keep talking, but I'd just be repeating myself with more hand gestures."
"Well. My social battery is officially dead."
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Can I trust you? I mean really. ...if that makes sense."
"That's the right answer. The wrong one would've been 'yes' too fast."
"I'll tell you what I tell everyone: watch what I do when nobody's watching. That's the whole of me. The rest is just talking."
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Still on whether they can trust you."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
They glance toward the fire, toward the others — checking who's listening.
A pause that's a beat too long. "I think you're confused," Ursula says, not quite looking at you.
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"Any regrets? The real kind, not the small stuff."
Quiet. "Yeah. I think everyone's carrying one of those."
"I regret the ordinary days I rushed through. All those Novosibirsk, Russia mornings I spent annoyed at small things. I'd pay anything for one annoyed morning now."
"Still on your regrets."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Good question." "That night — I stood down Night Court at the treeline — it ran. I keep hearing it when I try to sleep."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"My hands stopped shaking two days ago. I'm calling that healed."
"We lost the illusion that the treeline holds itself. That's a kind of progress."
You show them Ghost Pipe — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Hey — I found some Ghost Pipe today. You were right, it was right where you said."
Their whole posture softens around you.
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Mm. Still on that plant lesson."
"Sure — what's on your mind? That's the whole of it."
"Huh. Let me think about that." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "That night — I stood down White Noise at the treeline — it ran. I keep hearing it when I try to sleep."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Alright — I should get back to it."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
"This was good." They mean it.

"We never did finish talking about what's been happening — that was 11 days back. Still on your mind? 'You show them Ghost Pipe — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. I never knew that.'"
"Help me haul something back? Too much for one."
Dmitri shows you where they go to think. "Don't tell the others. Everyone needs one place."
"I show up. That's my part."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on what's been happening."
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"Good question." "I'd follow you out past the treeline. Don't tell the others — they'd want to come too."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"And... scene. Good talk."
"This was good." They mean it.
"What's the most useful thing you've learned since we got here?"
"The fundamental skill. Everything else is decoration."
"weather-reading. Sounds small. But small useful things stack — and one day you look up and you're the person everyone asks. That's how it happens."
"Still on the most useful thing you've learned."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up? It'll pass."
"Huh. Let me think about that." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "You saw it too, right? Hardened The Informant. Tell me I didn't imagine the lights."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to that foraging help."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."

deathBeat: d20: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Giuseppe Young is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d20: 🕯️ Giuseppe Young is dead — the wild. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d20: The village's quarrel was with Giuseppe — and Giuseppe is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
recoverHome: d21: That night, they bring Giuseppe home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.
vouch: d20: At the grave, Siobhan, Wanjiru speak for Aaron — "Giuseppe trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
systemVoice: d20: SYSTEM: Oh! It has a NAME. You all love names.
burialWindowSay: d20: The Highbeam Deer thrashes its antlers at you — getting close has a price.
d20: The Highbeam Deer thrashes its antlers at you — getting close has a price.
d20: The Highbeam Deer thrashes its antlers at you — getting close has a price.
d20: The village's quarrel was with Giuseppe — and Giuseppe is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d20: At the grave, Siobhan, Wanjiru speak for Aaron — "Giuseppe trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
d21: That night, they bring Giuseppe home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.
d23: You say a few words for Giuseppe. Not a ceremony — just: you were here, and someone noticed you leaving. (-3 trauma)
d23: You bury Giuseppe. A marker, of sorts. The village will know where. (+4 trauma)
echoSample: d23: "Giuseppe always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
d23: "You want to know about that? Okay." "Giuseppe owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
d27: "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Since Giuseppe died... I keep expecting to see Giuseppe at the fire. Stupid."
d27: "Nobody says Giuseppe's name right yet. We will. Give it a few days."
d27: "You want to know about that? Okay." "Last time things were different. They always are." "Giuseppe is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
echoV2Sample: d23: The village raises a marker by the fire — Giuseppe, day 23. the wild. A place to stand.
